items_missed: No agenda statement — never told the customer what the call would cover or how long it would take, and never asked 'sound good?' to confirm
Never asked for origin or destination address/zip — the entire quote rests on the customer's offhand 'maybe like five minutes' for drive distance
Never asked about stairs or floors at either home, on a 3-bedroom house quote
Never asked about access — parking, driveway, walk distance, HOA or gate restrictions
Never asked about additional stops or storage stops
Never asked the moving-stressors question ('anything you're particularly worried about with this move?')
Entire Save Your Ass prep speech skipped — no consolidation examples, no 'take a carload' tip, no 'prep = shorter move = lower bill' framing
No sense-check after the clock explanation ('does that make sense?')
Did not mention trucks — gave mover count (2) but never said how many trucks
China cabinet with removable glass shelves was noted but never explained as a time/handling variable in the estimate
Confirmation email mentioned but never explained — no bolded details list at the top, no 'reply with any corrections'
Never asked 'any other questions before I let you go?'
Never gave office hours or how to reach the team — customer said she'd 'call back' with no callback path offered
Used the customer's name only twice; also called her 'Alex' once mid-call
No 60¢/lb baseline given alongside the $2,000 No Worries coverage
top_strength: The inventory probe and the estimate reasoning were genuinely good — he walked room by room, caught the appliances and the Blackstone, then explained why a near-1800 sq ft home would normally be 3 movers for 8 hours but her furniture-only scope drops it to 2 movers at 4.5–5.5 hours. He also volunteered the 'if we finish in four hours flat, that's all you pay for' reassurance without being asked.
coaching_note: This was the single best Save Your Ass setup you'll get all week and he walked right past it. The customer volunteered that she's moving her own boxes to save money, is going five minutes down the road, and is still shopping quotes — she is explicitly cost-motivated. That is the exact moment for the prep speech: consolidate the toy room and the kids' stuff, drawers emptied, photos off the walls, take a carload yourself. It costs 60 seconds, it directly lowers her bill, and it is the differentiator that makes her stop collecting quotes. Second priority: he quoted a 3-bedroom move without ever asking about stairs, walk distance, or parking at either address — that is exactly the gap that shows up later as an estimate-accuracy miss.
phone_presence_notes: Polite and easy to talk to with light affirmations ('awesome', 'of course', 'cool'), but the pricing block ran as one long uninterrupted monologue, the customer's name was barely used and once got wrong, and no warmth was offered around the family details (crib, kids' playroom) she shared.
